findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, a property name that no browser ever implemented (IE10/11 used `-ms-flex-align`, which the mixin already emits on the line above). The line is dead output compiled into every stylesheet bundle that includes a flexbox call; the next maintainer debugging IE alignment will chase a vendor prefix that never had any effect, and the fabricated prefix pattern invites copy-paste into other mixins.

[ADVISORY] The mixins mix the 2009 old-spec (`display: -webkit-box`, `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`, `-webkit-box-align`) with the modern flexible-box spec (`order`, `align-items`, `flex`) in the same rule, but the two specs are not interchangeable: old-spec children need `box-flex` and old-spec `box-ordinal-group` numbering starts from 1 with different grouping semantics, so browsers falling back to the old spec render different layouts than modern browsers. Users on legacy WebKit/Gecko builds (the only reason the old-spec lines exist) get a header layout computed under 2009 box semantics — e.g. `.panel` with `margin-left: auto` is a no-op under `-moz-box`/`-webkit-box`, dropping the right-aligned hamburger/panel entirely while Chrome/Firefox show it correctly.

[ADVISORY] Making .contents a flex container silently changes layout for every child that previously relied on the float-based flow, and the diff only compensates for .title and .panel — the .valign-helper and any plugin/theme-inserted .contents children are unhandled. Plugin and theme components that append elements to .d-header .contents (e.g. custom header links, banners) render in DOM order with order:0, sliding between .title and the .extra-info-wrapper/.panel instead of stacking after them as the old float layout effectively did; header appearance breaks for those sites with no signal in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The align-items mixin emits -ms-flex-align: $alignment, but IE10's implementation supports only start/end/center/stretch/baseline (not flex-start/flex-end names), and -moz-box-align/-webkit-box-align accept only start|end|center|baseline|stretch — passing any modern value like flex-start makes the whole declaration invalid in those engines. Any future call site using align-items(flex-start) or align-items(flex-end) silently loses alignment in old-webkit/IE10 browsers while looking correct in evergreen browsers; the badges.css.scss baseline call in this diff is the only currently-safe value.

[ADVISORY] .small-action-desc padding changes from fixed 0.5em/4em (which cleared the 45px .topic-avatar) to percentage padding 0 1.5%, dropping the vertical padding entirely while the avatar keeps padding: 5px 0. Small-action rows that render without a topic-avatar child (deleted-by, auto-close notices where no avatar is emitted) previously had vertical breathing room from the 0.5em padding; now they sit flush against adjacent post rows, and the 1.5% horizontal padding scales with container width so narrow/mobile views get visibly less inset than the old 4em clearance.

[ADVISORY] .extra-info-wrapper keeps float: left on .badge-wrapper and gains order(2) + line-height: 1.5, but the diff removes the .bullet margin-top: 5px compensation without addressing that the wrapper is now an order-controlled flex item whose internal floats depend on the old vertical metrics. Topic-page header badges aligned via the old 5px bullet offset will sit misaligned relative to the other-title text in the new centered flex row on topic pages; nobody verified the topic-header badge/text baseline after the change.

[ADVISORY] The PR's stated intent is 'optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins,' but this diff restyles .small-action content spacing (padding 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em -> 0 1.5%, removal of margin-top: 5px, removal of p padding-top: 4px) with no header involvement. Reviewers and future maintainers get a visual regression in small-action blocks (deleted posts, closed notices) mixed silently into a performance-scoped PR; if the flexbox work needs reverting, these unrelated style changes revert with it or get lost, and nobody tracing 'header layout' requirements can account for them.

[ADVISORY] The align-items mixin emits -ms-align-items, which is not a real CSS property in any browser or flexbox spec era, so the new 'universal' mixin ships dead/invalid declarations. Any consumer of the mixin gets silently ignored -ms-align-items output in compiled CSS for IE10-era rendering; the invariant the mixin promises (cross-browser alignment) is not enforced for the old-IE code paths it was written for, and the invalid property propagates to every future call site.

[ADVISORY] @include order(2) is applied to .extra-info-wrapper and order(3) to .panel, but .contents' other flex children (e.g. .title, hamburger) get default order 0, meaning visual order depends on source order plus scattered order values across two files with no order(1) — the ordering invariant is only partially and implicitly enforced. The next contributor adding a child to .contents must reverse-engineer the implicit 0/2/3 ordering spread across header.scss and topic.scss to avoid misplacing their element; reordering work is spread across files with no single source of truth.

[BUG] The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment`, a property that has never existed in any browser, alongside the real IE10 property `-ms-flex-align`. The line is silently ignored by the CSS parser; any IE10 user gets no vertical alignment, and the next editor copying this mixin pattern perpetuates the dead property. It also indicates the prefix set was written from memory rather than verified, casting doubt on the other vendor blocks.

[BUG] The panel's right-alignment now relies on `margin-left: auto` inside the flex container, but the same mixin stack also emits the 2009/-ms-flexbox (IE10) display values where auto margins are not honored for main-axis alignment. On IE10 (a supported target for the prefixed stack this diff ships), .panel renders immediately after the title instead of flush right — the header layout the PR claims to preserve breaks on exactly the browsers the prefixes exist for.

[ADVISORY] The mixins mix three incompatible flexbox generations (-webkit-box/-moz-box 2009, -ms-flexbox 2012 draft, -webkit-flex final) while passing the same keyword arguments to each, but the old specs use different value vocabularies and unit systems (e.g. -moz-box-ordinal-group requires integer >= 1, -webkit-box-align accepts start/end not flex-start). Callers using flex-start/flex-end (the natural modern values) will silently misrender on the old-spec prefixes the mixin exists to serve; the abstraction presents one API over three divergent semantics.

[ADVISORY] The `.valign-helper` element (kept at line 17) exists solely to fake vertical centering under the old float layout, but with align-items(center) on .contents it is now dead weight and its inline-block baseline can still affect flex line layout. The zero-width helper remains in the DOM/CSS as a layout-affecting flex item; the next layout change must reason about an element whose purpose is gone.

[ADVISORY] `.small-action-desc` padding changed from the fixed `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` (where 4em matched the avatar column) to `0 1.5%`, making the indent relative to container width instead of the avatar size it visually belongs to. At narrow viewport widths the percentage padding shrinks below the avatar width so the description text underlaps the avatar, while at wide widths the gap grows disproportionately — the alignment invariant between desc and avatar, previously guaranteed by the shared em unit, is now unenforced.

[BUG] The PR titled as a flexbox 'performance' change silently alters small-action visual layout: `.small-action-desc` padding changes from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%` and `> p` loses its `padding-top: 4px`, plus `.topic-avatar` loses compensating margins. Users see visibly different spacing/indentation of small-action messages (e.g. topic closing notices) — a behavior/visual change shipped under a performance-optimization objective with no stated acceptance, and with no fallback if flexbox is unsupported (the 4em left padding that emulated avatar offset is now gone, so text will overlap/collide with the avatar column in non-flexbox browsers).

[BUG] `.extra-info-wrapper` gains `line-height: 1.5` and the `.badge-wrapper.bullet` `margin-top: 5px` compensation is deleted, changing rendered header appearance under a PR whose stated intent was only layout method performance. Topic header badge text vertical rhythm changes visually for all users; the deleted 5px bullet margin-top plus new line-height shifts badges out of baseline alignment with the title — a visual regression shipped without explicit acceptance that appearance would change.

[BUG] The `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment`, which is not a valid CSS property, so the declaration is discarded by every browser; IE10's real equivalent is `-ms-flex-align` (and 2009-spec `-webkit-box-align`/`-moz-box-align` also expect `start|end|center`, not `baseline`/`center` keyword values from the modern spec). In IE10 (ms-flexbox) and old WebKit/Mozilla flexbox browsers, `.small-action` and header rows silently fall back to `stretch`-like alignment and the intended `order(2)`/`order(3)` header arrangement breaks or misaligns, producing a visibly broken header with no error anywhere.

[ADVISORY] `.contents` becomes a flex container while `.valign-helper` (the old float-era vertical alignment hack) is retained untouched, leaving dead/contradictory structure in the new layout. The next maintainer editing header alignment must reason about both the flexbox path and the obsolete valign-helper hack; the stale hack also risks double-offset behavior as children of a flex container, making future header changes riskier.
